entry.title: The Billie Jean King Cup team surprises student athletes at Atlantic for an unforgettable day
entry.summary: While most kids in Palm Beach County are wrapping up their last few days before Thanksgiving Break, kids at Atlantic screamed at the top of their lungs when they met Coco Gauff and the Billie Jean King Cup team. WATCH: Billie Jean King Cup team visits Atlantic ahead of weekend showdown Billie Jean King Cup team visits Atlantic ahead of weekend showdown Ive never actually met any celebrities or professional athletes, so this is an eye-opening experience, said Mateo St. Edward, a senior volleyball player. Hundreds of student-athletes filled the auditorium at Atlantic High School, thanks to the U.S. Billie Jean King Cup team. This weekend, the ladies will face off against Hungary in a best-of-five playoff tie at the Delray Beach Tennis Center. Before they took the court, they stopped by to speak with young athletes; the kids chanted as the ladies of the Billie Jean King Cup team hit the stage and even got to ask some questions. It was so cool I was able to ask the coach I asked her where she would be if she werent a tennis player, and she said she'd be a teacher. So it was cool for the teachers to see she would be one of them, said fellow volleyball star, Ryan Jaber. Hilary Dorce, a star on the softball team, admits meeting all the women was more than an honor. It was very inspirational, especially since there were a lot of young women in front of me, especially being a young Black woman in sports. It really lifted my spirits and made me more confident, said Dorce. While the kids were taken aback, Coco Gauff had one more trick up her sleeve: she did the two-step with the students and created everlasting memories for them while feeling a sense of fulfillment for herself. It just means a lot to be back, and I didnt think they were going to care this much about tennis, but they do, so I was really impressed with the questions they asked and energy they brought, said Gauff. In addition to Gauff and her teammates' work, her grandmother, Yvonne Lee Odom, who became the first Black student to integrate the school then called Seacrest High School, was honored with a $10,000 scholarship in her name. It was thanks to Gainbridge and Bigger Than Sports, a youth-led nonprofit fighting educational inequality throughout. Well, Coco, thanks for coming home and making the kids' day. Now, make us proud this weekend.

entry.title: Hobe Sound singer gets surprise duet with 'Glee' star after FAA ground stop upends his show
entry.summary: Last week's FAA ground stop uprooted plans and wreaked havoc for so many people across the U.S. But for one Hobe Sound woman, it led to what could be her big break. WATCH: FAA ground stop leads to surprise duet for Hobe Sound singer in Jupiter FAA ground stop leads to surprise duet for Hobe Sound singer in Jupiter When the FAA grounded flights across the U.S., it cast a dark cloud over the Maltz Jupiter Theatre, where Broadway and 'Glee' star Matthew Morrison was scheduled to perform this weekend. Much of his ensemble couldn't make it here. But with storms come rainbows. And one local singer can attest. Emily Rynasko, who said she watched 'Glee' when she was younger, said she would have never expected a text from the actor who played William Schuester, asking her to sing a duet with him on stage. 'I found out about 9:30 in the morning, and the show was at 7:30 that night,' Emily Rynasko said. It was a moment Rynasko had been working toward her whole life. 'Learning sight-reading music and just using my ear. It's being a trained musician that's part of your job,' Rynasko said. Rynasko, who grew up in Hobe Sound, started that training as a kid at the Maltz Jupiter Theatre. 'They raised me. The Maltz Jupiter Theater is my, my home, and that is truly my family. They have made me the woman I am,' Rynasko said. So when Rynasko stepped into the spotlight to sing Somewhere Over the Rainbow, she treated it like a professional and felt right at home next to Morrison. 'I was a lot calmer than I thought I would be because I treated it like any other show that I had done,' Rynasko said. After all, there's no place like home. 'To also honor everyone that has been part of your journey, whether it's been a teacher, your community, your friends and family,' Rynasko said. 'That's what brings me joy and carries me through.' This story was reported on-air by journalist Jamie Ostroff and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: Flooded roads reported in Vero Lake Estates as Indian River County schools close - cw34.com
entry.summary: Flooded roads reported in Vero Lake Estates as Indian River County schools close    cw34.com
entry.article_text: The Indian River County Sheriff’s Office is reporting more flooded roads in the Vero Lake Estates area as heavy rain moves through the county Thursday. The sheriff’s office urged drivers to stay off flooded roads, warning that water can be deeper than it appears and can stall vehicles. High-water vehicles are in the area, and anyone who becomes stranded should call 911. Ryan Lloyd, Indian River County’s emergency management chief, told CBS12 News the county has received about 5 to 7 inches of rain so far. He said the north end of the county, including Sebastian, Fellsmere and Vero Lake Estates, has gotten more than the rest. Another 3 to 5 inches is expected by midnight Friday, Lloyd said, and the area is still at risk for pockets of 10 to 12 inches or more falling in a short time. Lloyd said the county’s water management systems are full and the ground is essentially saturated, so new rain is running off onto roads. The county’s emergency operations center is at a Level 2 partial activation, and National Guard members are there with high-water vehicles. Lloyd said there had been no requests for high-water rescues as of Thursday afternoon. He urged residents to avoid nonessential travel, turn around at flooded roads and never drive around barricades. Please do not drive to neighborhoods that are flooded because that can actually push floodwaters into homes and create a bigger problem than what some of those residents may already be facing, Lloyd said. The weather prompted the School District of Indian River County to close all public schools and district offices Thursday. The district said saturated ground and expected rain could make travel unsafe for students and staff. Lloyd said schools will also be closed Friday. A Vero Beach football game scheduled for Friday night has been moved to Saturday at 7 p.m., he said. CHIME IN: Send in your weather photos and videos The National Weather Service issued a flood advisory Thursday morning for eastern Indian River and northeastern St. Lucie counties, reporting that 2 to 4 inches of rain had fallen in parts of the area. The advisory warned of minor flooding in low-lying and poorly drained areas. A flood watch remains in effect for Indian River County through Friday evening, with more showers and thunderstorms possible. See also: Flood risk lingers across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beaches before a drier weekend The county’s road closure map , viewed at 2:47 p.m. Thursday, listed 13 road closures and six lane closures. Among the roads marked closed were 100th Court, 103rd Avenue, 104th Avenue, 83rd Street and 87th Street. The map also showed a long-term closure on 13th Street Southwest, scheduled to remain in place until Jan. Lane-closure listings included 101st Avenue, West 98th Avenue and two locations near Barber Street and U.S. The county also warned that heavy rain and gusty winds could disrupt trash collection. Residents whose streets are flooded were asked not to put carts in the water; the landfill and customer convenience centers could close early if conditions become unsafe. The City of Fellsmere also urged drivers to use extreme caution, identifying two potential trouble spots: New York Avenue near Hickory Street and North Broadway. The city said those roads could close if rain continues. City Hall remains open and operating normally. Lloyd said there are no known water main breaks or significant power outages in the county. The county’s Emergency Information Center, at 772-226-4000, will be open overnight Thursday for questions and flooding reports, and the county will decide Friday whether to keep it running. Residents can report flood damage to homes and businesses through the county’s emergency management website .

entry.title: Port St. Lucie hit-and-run victim dies; driver could face more serious charges - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie hit-and-run victim dies; driver could face more serious charges    WPEC
entry.article_text: The victim of a hit and run crash in Port St. Lucie has passed away, which could lead to more serious charges against the driver who police say hit her. The victim, Alexis Cuellar, 24, of Port St. Lucie was critically injured when she was hit while riding her e-scooter on her way to her job at a nearby Wendy's at about 5:10 in the morning on Monday, November 16. Police say Tristian Ray Sanchez-Chasmer, 18, of Port St. Lucie had been playing ding-dong-ditch with friends before the crash and the Chevy Tahoe he was driving hit Cuellar in a crosswalk at SW Feather Terrace and SW Gatlin Boulevard and he did not stop to check on her or render aid. He was charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury. A former prosecutor says it's likely Sanchez-Chasmer will now face a more serious charge of leaving the scene of a crash involving death, and he could also be charged with vehicular homicide. "Prosecutors will often file both. Leaving the scene involving death and vehicular homicide. Because they punish two different wrongs. One punishes how he drove, and the other punishes his decision to flee," said Dave Aronberg, former Palm Beach County State Attorney. He is now an attorney in private practice in West Palm Beach. See also: Flooded roads reported in Vero Lake Estates as Indian River County schools close "A lot of these cases take time because you've got to go through an exhaustive review to make sure you get it right, you know, to find out, was he speeding excessively? Was he blowing through stop signs? Was he driving erratically? They'll look at the black box inside the car, that's the event data recorder. They're gonna check to see braking. They'll check to see the marks on the road. They'll look to see the throttle position before impact," said Dave Aronberg, former Palm Beach County State Attorney. Aronberg says if those two charges are filed they would each carry a maximum penalty of 30 years in prison, which means Sanchez-Chasmer could potentially face up to 60 years in prison if convicted. "The next step is an exhaustive investigation. And I think prosecutors will upgrade the charge now that the victim has died.

entry.title: 18-year-old charged in Port St. Lucie hit-and-run that critically injured woman riding e-scooter - WFLX
entry.summary: 18-year-old charged in Port St. Lucie hit-and-run that critically injured woman riding e-scooter    WFLX
entry.article_text: An 18-year-old driver has been arrested after Port St. Lucie Police Department investigators say he struck a 24-year-old woman riding an electric scooter to work and left the scene, leaving her critically injured. Police say the driver had been playing a “ding-dong-ditch” prank with friends shortly before Monday morning’s crash. Police identified the driver as Tristan Sanchez-Chasmer. He was arrested on a felony charge of leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury, according to the department. The crash happened near Southwest Gatlin Boulevard and Southwest Feather Terrace. Investigators said the woman was traveling west on the sidewalk toward Southwest Rosser Boulevard and had entered a crosswalk when she was hit by a gray Chevrolet Tahoe making a left turn onto Southwest Feather Terrace. Lucie Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said Tuesday the woman remained unconscious and in critical condition. “We’re deeply concerned for her recovery, and our thoughts are with her loved ones,” Niemczyk said. Police said a witness stopped to help the woman, called 911 and was able to get the SUV’s license plate information. Investigators used that information to identify the vehicle and the driver. Investigators said Sanchez-Chasmer had two friends with him and had been playing “ding-dong-ditch” shortly before the crash. “They were specifically playing, I’ll call it ring and run, ding-dong-ditch, at a house that belonged to a friend of theirs, and apparently the mother came to the door and they fled the scene,” Niemczyk told WPTV. Niemczyk said investigators believe the people inside the SUV realized a collision had occurred. “They’re aware that they hit something. According to Niemczyk, Sanchez-Chasmer and the two passengers did not call 911. Niemczyk said the decision to leave the scene was key to the criminal investigation. “Had they remained on scene, provided aid, it would have been a very different criminal outcome,” Niemczyk said. “There probably wouldn’t have been criminal charges at that point.” Sanchez-Chasmer was charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury. According to published reports citing law enforcement records, he was being held on a $5,000 bond. Police have not announced charges against the two passengers. WFLX returned to the intersection after the crash and spoke with 15-year-old John Rogalewski, who said he rides an e-scooter to school and is sometimes on the road early in the morning. “I’m looking at my surroundings almost the whole time,” Rogalewski said. “I’m making sure every time I have to cross the street that there’s not a car coming up, and that it is my sign to go, no matter how long I have to wait to cross.” Police said the 24-year-old woman was wearing a helmet when she was struck. The investigation remains active, according to police, and toxicology results are still pending. entry.title: Martin County Teacher of the Year Richard Acosta celebrates educators who inspire students
entry.summary: Pinewood Elementary School science teacher Richard Acosta has been named the 2026-27 Martin County Teacher of the Year, earning the opportunity to represent the county in the Florida Department of Educations statewide Teacher of the Year competition. The Education Foundation of Martin County announced Acosta as the overall winner during its Teacher of the Year Award Celebration on Nov. 6 at the MIDFLORIDA Event Center in Port St. Lucie. Acosta was also named Elementary Teacher of the Year. This is phenomenal, Acosta said after the honor was revealed. I feel incredibly invigorated and inspired to go to the next level and represent Martin County at the state competition. Three educators represent Martin County schools Acosta was among three educators recognized with top honors. Miriam Hernndez, an intensive reading teacher at Indiantown Middle School, was named Middle School Teacher of the Year. Marc Turull, who teaches International Baccalaureate physics and chemistry at South Fork High School, was named High School Teacher of the Year. Turull said the award also represents the people he works alongside. Its such an honor, Turull said. I teach physics, and I work with amazing people, so to represent them and be Teacher of the Year makes me so grateful. Hernndez described the recognition as both a privilege and an honor. entry.article_text: Pinewood Elementary School science teacher Richard Acosta has been named the 2026-27 Martin County Teacher of the Year, earning the opportunity to represent the county in the Florida Department of Education’s statewide Teacher of the Year competition.The Education Foundation of Martin County announced Acosta as the overall winner during its Teacher of the Year Award Celebration on Nov. 6 at the MIDFLORIDA Event Center in Port St. Lucie.Acosta was also named Elementary Teacher of the Year.“This is phenomenal,” Acosta said after the honor was revealed. “I feel incredibly invigorated and inspired to go to the next level and represent Martin County at the state competition.”Acosta was among three educators recognized with top honors.Miriam Hernández, an intensive reading teacher at Indiantown Middle School, was named Middle School Teacher of the Year.Marc Turull, who teaches International Baccalaureate physics and chemistry at South Fork High School, was named High School Teacher of the Year.Turull said the award also represents the people he works alongside.“It’s such an honor,” Turull said. “I teach physics, and I work with amazing people, so to represent them and be Teacher of the Year makes me so grateful.”Hernández described the recognition as both a privilege and an honor.During the celebration, the three teachers emphasized the importance of educators at every stage of a student's education.“The fact is that it takes all three of us for excellence in Martin County schools,” Acosta said. “We start with the foundation in elementary school. We move on to middle school intensive reading, and then we finish at the high school at South Fork. So we, we feel very blessed to be working together.”The Education Foundation said Acosta’s 35-year career in education can be traced partly to his own experience as a teenager.According to the Education Foundation of Martin County, at 16, Acosta was struggling with confidence and direction when he entered teacher John Lynskey’s American history class. According to the foundation, Lynskey’s storytelling and encouragement helped Acosta develop a love of learning.Acosta still keeps two history books Lynskey gave him.His path toward teaching became clearer when Acosta later tutored a younger student after school and watched the child's confidence and enthusiasm for learning grow, according to the foundation.Today, Acosta teaches science to students from prekindergarten through fifth grade at Pinewood Elementary.“I love what I do, and I love energizing the classroom and engaging them to the greatest possibility,” Acosta said.His lessons include hands-on investigations tied to the natural environment around Martin County. The Education Foundation said students have examined sea turtle skull models, shells and other materials connected to the Indian River Lagoon while studying how adaptations help turtles survive.Acosta also helped develop a “Birds of the Everglades” curriculum with environmental partners and has been involved with schoolwide science initiatives and family STEAM events.For Acosta, the recognition provides another opportunity beyond representing Martin County at the state level.“I feel very blessed to be in this position because I get to mentor other teachers from other schools,” Acosta said.Acosta also receives a one-year vehicle lease provided through Audi Stuart and Infiniti Stuart.“That is amazing and spectacular,” Acosta said. “I cannot wait to pick out a car on Saturday.”The celebration recognized 24 school-level Teachers of the Year who were selected by their peers. According to the Education Foundation, nominees submitted application portfolios and participated in interviews before a panel of judges.Felix A. Williams Elementary School also won the Spirit Award for its enthusiasm, interpretation of the event's theme, and props.The recognition comes as Martin County educators continue the everyday work behind the awards: helping children learn, building their confidence and creating connections that can influence students long after they leave the classroom.For Acosta, that circle is especially meaningful. A teacher once helped him see greater possibilities for his own future. Decades later, he is working to create those possibilities for another generation.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.summary: The Defense Health Agency has authorized temporary emergency prescription refills for TRICARE beneficiaries in 20 Florida counties affected by fall flooding. The waiver remains in effect through Nov. 29. The counties covered by the waiver are Brevard, Broward, DeSoto, Duval, Flagler, Glades, Hardee, Hendry, Highlands, Indian River, Martin, Miami-Dade, Monroe, Okeechobee, Palm Beach, Putnam, Seminole, St. Johns, St. Lucie and Volusia. How TRICARE beneficiaries can get emergency refills Beneficiaries who need an emergency refill should take their prescription bottle to any TRICARE retail network pharmacy, according to the Defense Health Agency. If the prescription bottle is unavailable or its label is damaged or missing, beneficiaries should contact Express Scripts or a retail network pharmacy for assistance. Beneficiaries can find a network pharmacy through the A potentially unsafe link has been removed or by calling Express Scripts at 1-877-363-1303. When possible, beneficiaries should visit the pharmacy where the prescription was originally filled. Prescriptions filled by a retail chain may also be filled at another location operated by the same chain. If the prescribing clinician is available, beneficiaries can also ask the clinician to call a new prescription into a network pharmacy. Urgent and emergency care during flooding TRICARE beneficiaries other than active-duty service members may receive urgent care from any TRICARE-authorized urgent care center or provider without a referral, according to the Defense Health Agency. entry.title: PSL police have a GTA VI release-day warning: Port St. Lucie is not Vice City - cw34.com
entry.summary: PSL police have a GTA VI release-day warning: Port St. Lucie is not Vice City    cw34.com
entry.article_text: The wanted level in Port St. Lucie should stay at zero, police say. As Grand Theft Auto VI arrives Thursday, the Port St. Lucie Police Department posted a playful safety briefing reminding fans that real life doesn’t come with a respawn button and that U.S. 1 and Crosstown are not racetracks. Five stars might be impressive in GTA , but trust us, you don’t want that kind of attention in Port St. Lucie, the department wrote. Its other reminders: patrol vehicles aren’t available for test drives, red lights aren’t suggestions, sidewalks aren’t shortcuts and the SWAT team isn’t a feature anyone wants to unlock. What happens in Vice City stays in Vice City, the post said. Lucie might come with a police report. The game officially launches Nov. 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar’s fictional state of Leonida draws on Florida , with Vice City serving as its Miami-inspired centerpiece. The game follows Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, whose criminal plans pull them into a conspiracy spanning the state. CBS12 has been following the Sunshine State’s transformation into a real-life part of the game’s promotion. In September, a giant pink Welcome to Vice City sign went up on Miami’s Kaseya Center as part of a deal between Miami-Dade County and Rockstar Games. County officials said the arrangement was expected to bring in nearly $1 million in revenue and create marketing opportunities. Miami has also leaned into the Vice City connection with release-week events. The Miami Heat held a Night in Vice City celebration Wednesday, the night before launch. A release-day party is planned Thursday at the Clevelander South Beach, and Rockstar’s GTA VI : The Festival is scheduled for Saturday, Nov. See also: Who’s responsible for improving drainage after St. Lucie County’s historic flooding? Police in other cities have also used the GTA VI release to remind players to keep the game’s crime on screen. The Atlanta Police Department posted that GTA is not a real place, but Atlanta is! and warned that reckless driving, drunk driving, auto theft and violence have real consequences. Keep it in the game, the department wrote . In South Florida, law enforcement leaders raised a different concern before release day. The Miami-Dade Association of Chiefs of Police opposed plans to promote the county as Vice City, saying the game depicts violence against women and law enforcement. Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz also questioned whether public agencies should promote a game built around crimes her department works to prevent. For drivers tempted to bring a little of the game’s chaos onto local roads, PSLPD’s advice is simpler: drive safe, play smart and leave the wanted level in the game. Could 'sick days' coincide with release? The release could affect more than gamers’ free time. A GameSquare survey of 1,000 U.S. employees found that 10% of full-time employees surveyed who identify as gamers planned to skip work on launch day, while another 30% were considering taking time off. Of those considering time off, 36% said they would call in sick. The survey also found that 42% expected the game to make them less productive at work. Surveyed gamers expected to spend about $400 on the game and related purchases, and anticipated playing a median of 15 hours during the opening weekend. The survey found 70% might skip watching sports to spend more time gaming, while 42% said they’d be less likely to watch NFL games that weekend. I ndian River County students have Thursday off , giving young GTA VI fans an unexpected chance to spend part of release day in Vice City. The district closed schools because of forecast conditions and flooding concerns, while St. Lucie schools reopened and Palm Beach County schools remained open, except for West Boca High School, which is closed because of heavy flooding in the parking lot.

entry.article_text: Home Business News and Economic Updates in Sebastian, Florida Indian River County remains under Flood Watch as more rain possible by Andy Hodges Nov 19, 2026 / 5:51 PM A A A A Reset Indian River County remains under a Flood Watch Share on Twitter Share via Email INDIAN RIVER COUNTY — Indian River County remains under a Flood Watch, with a continued risk of excessive rainfall through Saturday, the National Weather Service said Thursday. There is a medium chance — 40% to 60% — of 3 to 6 inches of additional rainfall along the east-central Florida coast through Saturday, according to the National Weather Service office in Melbourne. Because the soil is already saturated from recent heavy rain, many areas are more prone to flooding. Officials said precise locations of the heaviest rainfall remain uncertain. If the most likely rainfall totals materialize, scattered pockets of flooding may develop along the coast, the forecast said. There is a 10% chance of higher-end totals of 8 to 10 inches or more in some locations. Those amounts would bring a risk of impactful flash flooding. The Indian River County Emergency Operations Center continues to monitor weather and road conditions. Officials urged residents to stay home if they do not need to travel. Floodwater and road damage can be difficult to see after dark, the EOC said. Residents should check the county’s road closure map before traveling and never drive through flooded roadways or around barricades. A road may be unsafe even if it is not shown as closed on the map. Multiple roads in the Vero Lake Estates area and elsewhere in the county have already seen closures or standing water this week because of the saturated ground. entry.title: Man accused of firing shots from West Palm Beach apartment balcony
entry.summary: A man is facing a misdemeanor charge after police say he fired shots from the balcony of a West Palm Beach apartment. Police said the incident began around 6:32 p.m. when children in the area approached an officer on patrol and reported hearing popping sounds. The officer located the apartment where the sounds were believed to have originated and directed a man and woman inside to come outside. According to police, both appeared to be intoxicated. Officers found shell casings and determined the man had fired shots from the apartment balcony. A police K-9 team was called to assist officers in clearing the scene. Police said firearms were found and recovered inside the apartment. The man was taken to a local hospital for treatment. Police did not provide details about why he required medical treatment. He was given a court date on a misdemeanor charge of discharging a firearm in public. Police said the investigation remains active and that authorities are exploring a risk protection order. Risk protection orders can temporarily restrict a person's access to firearms through a court process. Authorities said there is no threat to the public. entry.title: Psychological evaluation finds Thomas Markle competent to proceed in federal case
entry.summary: An independent psychological evaluation found Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, competent to proceed in the federal criminal case against him. The evaluation was conducted Nov. 16 and was the focus of a competency hearing Thursday in federal court in Tampa. After asking for additional time to consult with Thomas Markle, his attorney ultimately told the court the defense would not contest the evaluation's conclusion for purposes of the proceedings in Tampa. Watch report from Jada Williams: Psychological evaluation finds Thomas Markle competent to proceed in federal case The hearing briefly recessed after his defense attorney, Mary Claire Wolf, said more time was needed to speak with Thomas Markle about how to proceed. When court resumed roughly 30 minutes later, the defense declined to contest the competency finding and the psychological report was admitted into evidence. Wolf stressed that the decision should not be interpreted as Thomas Markle accepting the criminal allegations against him. She said the competency decision'has nothing to do with not disputing allegations against him,' adding that Thomas Markle 'vehemently denies' the allegations. The defense also indicated the competency issue could potentially be raised again once the case moves to California. Markle's daughter Samantha was inside the courtroom. She blew kisses to the camera following the hearing. When asked about the proceedings, she responded it was 'fine.' Markle's daughter Samantha was inside the courtroom Federal investigation leads to charge Thomas Markle, 82, faces one federal count of possession of child pornography. According to the criminal complaint, investigators learned in October that suspected child sexual abuse material, or CSAM, had allegedly been discovered among Thomas Markle's possessions in the Philippines. Investigators were later directed to storage units in the Los Angeles area. FBI agents obtained search warrants and seized approximately 78 items, including slides, film negatives and books containing suspected CSAM, according to federal authorities. The affidavit describes images investigators allege depict prepubescent girls and says some photographs appeared to show Thomas Markle with children in various stages of undress. MORE: Judge jails Thomas Markle, father of Meghan, after he cut off his ankle monitor The allegations have not been proven in court. Thomas Markle is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonab

entry.title: Port St. Lucie hit-and-run victim dies; driver could face more serious charges - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie hit-and-run victim dies; driver could face more serious charges    WPEC
entry.article_text: The victim of a hit and run crash in Port St. Lucie has passed away, which could lead to more serious charges against the driver who police say hit her. The victim, Alexis Cuellar, 24, of Port St. Lucie was critically injured when she was hit while riding her e-scooter on her way to her job at a nearby Wendy's at about 5:10 in the morning on Monday, November 16. Police say Tristian Ray Sanchez-Chasmer, 18, of Port St. Lucie had been playing ding-dong-ditch with friends before the crash and the Chevy Tahoe he was driving hit Cuellar in a crosswalk at SW Feather Terrace and SW Gatlin Boulevard and he did not stop to check on her or render aid. He was charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury. A former prosecutor says it's likely Sanchez-Chasmer will now face a more serious charge of leaving the scene of a crash involving death, and he could also be charged with vehicular homicide. "Prosecutors will often file both. Leaving the scene involving death and vehicular homicide. Because they punish two different wrongs. One punishes how he drove and the other punishes his decision to flee," said Dave Aronberg, former Palm Beach County State Attorney. He is now an attorney in private practice in West Palm Beach. See also: Flooded roads reported in Vero Lake Estates as Indian River County schools close "A lot of these cases take time because you've got to go through an exhaustive review to make sure you get it right, you know, to find out was he speeding excessively? Was he blowing through stop signs? Was he driving erratically? They'll look at the black box inside the car. That's the event data recorder. They're gonna check to see braking. They'll check to see the marks on the road. They'll look to see the throttle position before impact," Aronberg said. Aronberg says if those two charges are filed, leaving the scene of an accident involving death and vehicular homicide, they would each carry a maximum penalty of 30 years in prison, which means Sanchez-Chasmer could potentially face up to 60 years in prison if convicted. "The next step is an exhaustive investigation and I think prosecutors will upgrade the charge now that the victim has died. This is the latest crime involving kids playing ding dong ditch. It just, you wonder, how long is this gonna continue until they realize that nothing good can come of it? It just creates mass chaos and doesn't help anyone," Aronberg said.

entry.title: 'It rips your heart': Volunteers help Jensen Beach neighborhood recover from flood damage - WPBF
entry.summary: 'It rips your heart': Volunteers help Jensen Beach neighborhood recover from flood damage    WPBF
entry.article_text: Two weeks after floodwaters damaged homes in the Skyline Drive neighborhood of Jensen Beach, volunteers are working to help families recover and rebuild. Volunteers from Project LIFT and community partners arrived Thursday morning to assist with cleanup efforts. Stephen Leighton, with 25 United Disaster Relief, is the volunteer coordinator. "So earlier today the drywall was in this house. And you can see the waterline that is bled through to the studs," Leighton said. Video from the previous day showed drywall still in place, but volunteers, working alongside the organization 25 United, have since removed it. "So, Project LIFT, working with 25 United, came in, took all the drywall off the walls, took it outside to the dumpster," Leighton said. Dumpsters in the area are quickly filling up as the cleanup continues. "The whole house is empty. You see it now, what this team is doing, because we call it the Wrecking Crew," Leighton said. Leighton explained that county inspectors are assisting homeowners by providing guidance on necessary repairs and permits. He noted that 17 homes in the community had water damage, and some families are currently staying with friends or in hotels. We got Thanksgiving next week. Not that they’re going to be back in their home, but some sort of living needs to take place," Leighton said. Residents are still grappling with the aftermath of the flooding. Susan Destafney can't live in her home right now because of the water damage, and it's completely gutted. "We have a long way to go until we rebuild, you know. We’ve demoed, and we’ve got a long future ahead of us, and I know that God will be there for us and everything is going to be good," Destafney said. Mark Burner, who has lived in the neighborhood for 40 years, expressed gratitude for the volunteers. I never saw my wife cry so much, but you know what we did, though? We believe in God, we’re a community, and we’re going to make it," Burner said. The CEO of Project LIFT, Bob Zaccheo, emphasized that the work is about more than just removing damaged materials. "To see these houses getting repaired and torn apart, torn down, is one thing, but built back is a whole other," Zaccheo said. Leighton added that the efforts are being coordinated with state and federal representatives, with the goal of completing demolition and cleanup by Saturday. entry.title: Delray Beach Arts, Inc. takes step to bring back St. Patrick's Day Parade
entry.summary: Delray Beach Arts, Inc. has submitted an application to put on the 59th Annual Delray Beach St. Patrick's Day Parade after a new Florida law prompted the city to announce it would cancel the event. The nonprofit submitted the Special Event application in hopes of being granted permission to the parade in 2027. New legislation restricts local governments from funding, promoting or taking official actions related to certain diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) activities. Delray Beach Arts said that bringing the parade to life will require community support from sponsors, businesses, and community participation. They created a GoFundMe campaign and said they are actively seeking corporate sponsors and community partners for the event. 'Together, we can keep the tradition alive and make the 59th Annual Delray Beach St. Patricks Day Parade a celebration our community can be proud of,' the nonprofit said. When we spoke with Delray Beach Mayor Tom Carney earlier this month, he said he's confident the St. Patrick's Day Parade will go on as scheduled in 2027. Senate Bill 1143 takes effect Jan. 1, 2027.

entry.title: Man accused of firing shots from West Palm Beach apartment balcony
entry.summary: A man is facing a misdemeanor charge after police say he fired shots from the balcony of a West Palm Beach apartment. Police said the incident began around 6:32 p.m. at the Ibis Reserve Apartments when children in the area approached an officer on patrol and reported hearing popping sounds. The officer located the apartment where the sounds were believed to have originated and directed a man and woman inside to come outside. According to police, both appeared to be intoxicated. Officers found shell casings and determined the man had fired shots from the apartment balcony. A police K-9 team was called to assist officers in clearing the scene. Police said firearms were found and recovered inside the apartment. The man was taken to a local hospital for treatment. Police did not provide details about why he required medical treatment. He was given a court date on a misdemeanor charge of discharging a firearm in public. Police said the investigation remains active and that authorities are exploring a risk protection order. Risk protection orders can temporarily restrict a person's access to firearms through a court process. Authorities said there is no threat to the public. entry.title: Amendment 3 task force tries to get the message to Florida residents
entry.summary: Indian River Countys Tax Collector and Property Appraiser have formed Task Force 3, to get the word out for residents to qualify the new Homestead Exemption coming with Amendment 3. What people really need to understand is, there's less than five weeks to get a driver's license to become a resident of the state of Florida, said Property Appraiser Wesley Davis. WATCH: Amendment 3 task force tries to get the message to Florida residents Indian River Co Launches Amendment 3 Task Force Florida residency is a key component to being able to qualify for the exemption, which is rising to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, after voters approved the referendum on election day. New homeowners coming into the state after January 1, 2027 will have to wait five years for the new full exemptions. Current renters in Florida can still qualify for the new exemption on any future home they buy. The sense of urgency right now is that you don't need to have a homestead by the end of the year, Davis says. What you need to do to qualify for the homestead exemption is you must be a resident of the state of Florida by the end of the year.' That also includes current residents who have failed to get a Florida ID and still hold a driver's license from their previous state, says Tax Collector Carole Jean Jordan. They can establish residency in an apartment, and then when they buy a home, they can file for homestead. The local officials also pointed out county offices will be closed around the upcoming holidays. The impact of Amendment 3 will be felt in future county budgets, and both department heads acknowledge there are already discussions about budgeting next year. Estimates are that the county could lose about 20-30 million dollars over the first couple of years under the amendment. This will not end property taxes, Davis says. About half of everybody's tax bill goes to education, and education is not affected by this at all.

entry.title: Judge allows Hillsborough school bus camera lawsuit to proceed
entry.summary: A Hillsborough County judge has refused to throw out a lawsuit challenging the way drivers' ticket appeals are handled for Florida's controversial school bus cameras and the attorneys behind the case now want it to move forward on behalf of potentially thousands of other drivers. WATCH: Judge allows Hillsborough school bus camera lawsuit to proceed SCHOOL BUS CAMERA CLASS ACTION LAWSUIT FOLO The school bus stop arm cameras are designed to protect kids getting on and off school buses. But since they started rolling, Investigative Reporter Katie LaGrone and photojournalist Matthew Apthorp have exposed problems with what happens when drivers get a ticket and try to fight back. Stanley Shultz of Plant City was fined $225 last year after a school bus camera caught him passing the bus after its stop arm deployed. He said the bus' warning lights never flashed. So Shultz tried to challenge his violation and lost bringing his total fine to $270. But he's not done fighting, and neither is his attorney. 'He challenged the merits of the ticket. We're challenging the procedure,' said Shultz's attorney Gino Moreno. At issue: When a driver challenges one of these violations, who decides if it should be upheld or dismissed? Florida law calls for a 'local hearing officer' appointed by the school district or county. But in Hillsborough County, contested cases are being sent to state administrative judges through the Division of Administrative Hearings or DOAH and in most of these cases, the judges aren't in the same county where the ticket was issued. In Shultz's appeal, the judge who heard his appeal was in Tallahassee. And that's against the law, according to Shultz's lawsuit. 'If you're saying that it has to be heard by a local hearing officer, the hearing officer is being described as local. A state agency in Tallahassee is not local,' Moreno said. The Hillsborough County School District and its camera vendor, BusPatrol, tried to get the case dismissed. But recently, a judge said no, giving the green light for this camera lawsuit to keep rolling. Shultz's attorneys are now asking the court to certify the case as a class action, since there are thousands of other drivers in Hillsborough County whose appeals were also heard by judges outside the county. A state agency in Tallahassee is not local," Moreno said.The Hillsborough County School District and its camera vendor, BusPatrol, tried to get the case dismissed. For nearly two years, LaGrone and Apthorp have exposed problems with these cameras, which have generated nearly $30 million in paid fines in Hillsborough County alone.First, they discovered drivers were getting ticketed without a way to contest their fine. Then lawmakers had to adjust the law just to ensure drivers could appeal.It could take several months before a judge determines whether to certify this lawsuit as a class action. While this court battle is based in Hillsborough County, Moreno could expand the lawsuit to other Florida counties where DOAH judges are also being used to hear driver appeals.BusPatrol did not respond to our request for comment about this latest ruling but a spokesperson previously called the lawsuit "baseless." A spokesperson for the Hillsborough County school district said it does not comment on pending litigation. Shultz's attorney calls the lawsuit necessary for drivers to get a fair shot at fighting back what these buses capture on camera."You opened up this program before you set up a hearing program, then you changed the law, and then you still can't follow the law. That's ultimately what our position is: just get it right," Moreno said.

entry.title: Flooded roads reported in Vero Lake Estates as Indian River County schools close - WPEC
entry.summary: Flooded roads reported in Vero Lake Estates as Indian River County schools close    WPEC
entry.article_text: The Indian River County Sheriff’s Office is reporting more flooded roads in the Vero Lake Estates area as heavy rain moves through the county Thursday. The sheriff’s office urged drivers to stay off flooded roads, warning that water can be deeper than it appears and can stall vehicles. High-water vehicles are in the area, and anyone who becomes stranded should call 911. Ryan Lloyd, Indian River County’s emergency management chief, told CBS12 News the county has received about 5 to 7 inches of rain so far. He said the north end of the county, including Sebastian, Fellsmere and Vero Lake Estates, has gotten more than the rest. Another 3 to 5 inches is expected by midnight Friday, Lloyd said, and the area is still at risk for pockets of 10 to 12 inches or more falling in a short time. Lloyd said the county’s water management systems are full and the ground is essentially saturated, so new rain is running off onto roads. The county’s emergency operations center is at a Level 2 partial activation, and National Guard members are there with high-water vehicles. Lloyd said there had been no requests for high-water rescues as of Thursday afternoon. He urged residents to avoid nonessential travel, turn around at flooded roads and never drive around barricades. Please do not drive to neighborhoods that are flooded because that can actually push floodwaters into homes and create a bigger problem than what some of those residents may already be facing, Lloyd said. The weather prompted the School District of Indian River County to close all public schools and district offices Thursday. The district said saturated ground and expected rain could make travel unsafe for students and staff. Lloyd said schools will also be closed Friday. A Vero Beach football game scheduled for Friday night has been moved to Saturday at 7 p.m., he said. CHIME IN: Send in your weather photos and videos The National Weather Service issued a flood advisory Thursday morning for eastern Indian River and northeastern St. Lucie counties, reporting that 2 to 4 inches of rain had fallen in parts of the area. The advisory warned of minor flooding in low-lying and poorly drained areas. A flood watch remains in effect for Indian River County through Friday evening, with more showers and thunderstorms possible. See also: Flood risk lingers across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beaches before a drier weekend The county’s road closure map , viewed at 2:47 p.m. Thursday, listed 13 road closures and six lane closures. Among the roads marked closed were 100th Court, 103rd Avenue, 104th Avenue, 83rd Street and 87th Street. The map also showed a long-term closure on 13th Street Southwest, scheduled to remain in place until Jan. Lane-closure listings included 101st Avenue, West 98th Avenue and two locations near Barber Street and U.S. The county also warned that heavy rain and gusty winds could disrupt trash collection. Residents whose streets are flooded were asked not to put carts in the water; the landfill and customer convenience centers could close early if conditions become unsafe. The City of Fellsmere also urged drivers to use extreme caution, identifying two potential trouble spots: New York Avenue near Hickory Street and North Broadway. The city said those roads could close if rain continues. City Hall remains open and operating normally. Lloyd said there are no known water main breaks or significant power outages in the county. The county’s Emergency Information Center, at 772-226-4000, will be open overnight Thursday for questions and flooding reports, and the county will decide Friday whether to keep it running. Residents can report flood damage to homes and businesses through the county’s emergency management website .

entry.title: Woman dies after Port St. Lucie hit-and-run; police say driver was playing 'ding dong ditch' beforehand - WFLX
entry.summary: Woman dies after Port St. Lucie hit-and-run; police say driver was playing 'ding dong ditch' beforehand    WFLX
entry.article_text: A 24-year-old woman has died from injuries she suffered after she was struck while riding an electric scooter in a hit-and-run crash in Port St. Lucie , police said Wednesday. The woman died at approximately 9:23 p.m. Tuesday, according to the Port St. The crash happened around 5:10 a.m. Monday near the intersection of Southwest Gatlin Boulevard and Southwest Feather Terrace. Police said the woman was riding an electric scooter when a vehicle struck her. Investigators allege the driver left the scene without stopping to help her or notify law enforcement. The department’s Traffic Homicide Investigations Unit later identified the vehicle as a gray Chevrolet Tahoe and located it at a Port St. Lucie home, according to police. Investigators identified the alleged driver as 18-year-old Tristan Sanchez-Chasmer. Police said investigators learned Sanchez-Chasmer had been playing “ding dong ditch” with friends shortly before the crash. According to the department, the group was leaving a home where they had been participating in the prank when the vehicle struck the woman. Sanchez-Chasmer was arrested and charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury, a second-degree felony, police said. Following the woman’s death, police said they anticipate the State Attorney’s Office will pursue enhanced or additional charges as appropriate based on the circumstances and the outcome of the investigation. Police did not identify the woman in Wednesday’s news release.

entry.title: Vero Beach residents face another round of rising water - WFLX
entry.summary: Vero Beach residents face another round of rising water    WFLX
entry.article_text: Residents in Indian River County are dealing with another round of flooding, with approximately 12 roads closed Thursday evening and the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office urging drivers to stay off the roads as water continues to impact neighborhoods. The latest flooding comes just weeks after another round of high water left parts of the Treasure Coast struggling with similar conditions. Residents say this time, however, some neighborhoods appear to have fared better. For Terry Holly, who moved to the area from Pennsylvania with his wife 23 years ago, the flooding is an unwelcome reminder of what comes with living in Florida. “I escaped the snow to this,” Holly said. Water has surrounded parts of his neighborhood, Vero Lake Estates, leaving some residents with limited ways to get around. “We’re stuck another week. Luckily, we’ve got plenty of groceries and water, so we’re all set,” Holly said. Holly said he and other residents previously dropped their flood insurance policies. But after experiencing repeated flooding, he is reconsidering that decision. And we haven’t had it since, but now I’m going to rethink it again,” he said. County officials report multiple road closures along Vero Lake Estates. The Sheriff’s Office is urging drivers to avoid unnecessary travel and stay off flooded roads. Holly said he has not seen vehicles become stranded during this latest round of flooding, unlike the previous event. However, he warned that smaller vehicles may struggle to get through standing water. “The trucks and the high vehicles can get through. The small cars, forget it,” he said. Marjorie Hale said she believes this round of flooding has been handled better than the previous one, with more precautions being taken. But she is concerned about drivers who continue traveling too quickly through flooded neighborhoods. “You’ve got a lot of people who just don’t know how to drive in floodwaters,” Hale said. She also worries about the impact waves from passing vehicles can have on nearby homes, particularly older properties. Hale’s neighborhood experienced flooding during the previous round, too. A comparison of conditions outside her home then and now shows how the water has changed. She said drivers should slow down and consider the people living along those flooded streets. Indian River County Public Schools will be closed Friday as flooding continues to affect the area. For some families, the closure means an early start to Thanksgiving break. Hale said her daughter is old enough to stay home while she goes to work. She is also trying to find some humor in the situation. “We get our own private island. That’s what happens when it floods 6 inches of rainfall,” Hale said. Even her dog knows to be cautious around the water. He doesn’t wander off because he’s not willing to get in the floodwaters. While some residents are finding ways to make the best of the situation, Hale recognizes that other families across the Treasure Coast are dealing with more serious flooding and damage to their homes. Her message to the community is simple: look out for one another. “Invite your neighbors to Thanksgiving,” Hale said. She hopes the latest flooding will bring people together, especially those who may need a helping hand. “So let’s join together as a community,” she said. entry.summary: CBS12 News Athlete of the Week: Vero Beach's Latravious Woods Chases State Championship    WPEC
entry.article_text: From cheering in the stands to making big plays under the Friday night lights, Latravious Woods is living out his childhood dream. The Vero Beach High School wide receiver now plays for the same Fighting Indians team he grew up watching. But the junior has an even bigger goal: bringing a state championship home. See Also: Tennis Star Coco Gauff Returns Home for Billie Jean King Cup Since joining the team as a freshman, Woods has grown into a key playmaker and leader his coaches and teammates can count on, both on and off the field. "He's a guy that you hope to get the ball in his hands, however it needs to happen," Fighting Indians Head Coach Lenny Jankowski said. "And he's got some position versatility." Woods has also embraced his leadership role. "I know a lot about the program and how things and how coaches want things done," Woods said. "I just make sure everybody's just up-notch and like we all on the same level. Nobody heads down." Last week, Woods delivered another big performance, racking up more than 100 total yards and two touchdowns in Vero Beach's playoff win over Fort Pierce Central. But his impact goes beyond the stat sheet. Even when the ball isn't coming his way, Woods makes sure he's giving everything he has. "Even though I don't have the ball in my hands, I just got to go 100% every play because, you know, if I was to have the ball in my hand, I would want somebody to go 100% for me," Woods said. "So I'm going to give 100% for my teammates and my coaches because I want the same when I have the ball." After making the playoffs in all three of his high school seasons and reaching the state championship in 2025, Woods has unfinished business. He's determined to help Vero Beach take that final step, but he's keeping his focus on one game at a time. "Being back there this year and just finishing it all the way this time, it would feel so great," Woods said. "And I know the whole Vero community would love it." entry.title: PSL police have a GTA VI release-day warning: Port St. Lucie is not Vice City - WPEC
entry.summary: PSL police have a GTA VI release-day warning: Port St. Lucie is not Vice City    WPEC
entry.article_text: The wanted level in Port St. Lucie should stay at zero, police say. As Grand Theft Auto VI arrives Thursday, the Port St. Lucie Police Department posted a playful safety briefing reminding fans that real life doesn’t come with a respawn button and that U.S. 1 and Crosstown are not racetracks. Five stars might be impressive in GTA , but trust us, you don’t want that kind of attention in Port St. Lucie, the department wrote. Its other reminders: patrol vehicles aren’t available for test drives, red lights aren’t suggestions, sidewalks aren’t shortcuts and the SWAT team isn’t a feature anyone wants to unlock. What happens in Vice City stays in Vice City, the post said. Lucie might come with a police report. The game officially launches Nov. 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar’s fictional state of Leonida draws on Florida , with Vice City serving as its Miami-inspired centerpiece. The game follows Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, whose criminal plans pull them into a conspiracy spanning the state. CBS12 has been following the Sunshine State’s transformation into a real-life part of the game’s promotion. In September, a giant pink Welcome to Vice City sign went up on Miami’s Kaseya Center as part of a deal between Miami-Dade County and Rockstar Games. County officials said the arrangement was expected to bring in nearly $1 million in revenue and create marketing opportunities. Miami has also leaned into the Vice City connection with release-week events. The Miami Heat held a Night in Vice City celebration Wednesday, the night before launch. A release-day party is planned Thursday at the Clevelander South Beach, and Rockstar’s GTA VI : The Festival is scheduled for Saturday, Nov. See also: Who’s responsible for improving drainage after St. Lucie County’s historic flooding? Police in other cities have also used the GTA VI release to remind players to keep the game’s crime on screen. The Atlanta Police Department posted that GTA is not a real place, but Atlanta is! and warned that reckless driving, drunk driving, auto theft and violence have real consequences. Keep it in the game, the department wrote . In South Florida, law enforcement leaders raised a different concern before release day. The Miami-Dade Association of Chiefs of Police opposed plans to promote the county as Vice City, saying the game depicts violence against women and law enforcement. Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz also questioned whether public agencies should promote a game built around crimes her department works to prevent. For drivers tempted to bring a little of the game’s chaos onto local roads, PSLPD’s advice is simpler: drive safe, play smart and leave the wanted level in the game. Could 'sick days' coincide with release? The release could affect more than gamers’ free time. A GameSquare survey of 1,000 U.S. employees found that 10% of full-time employees surveyed who identify as gamers planned to skip work on launch day, while another 30% were considering taking time off. Of those considering time off, 36% said they would call in sick. The survey also found that 42% expected the game to make them less productive at work. Surveyed gamers expected to spend about $400 on the game and related purchases, and anticipated playing a median of 15 hours during the opening weekend. The survey found 70% might skip watching sports to spend more time gaming, while 42% said they’d be less likely to watch NFL games that weekend. I ndian River County students have Thursday off , giving young GTA VI fans an unexpected chance to spend part of release day in Vice City. The district closed schools because of forecast conditions and flooding concerns, while St. Lucie schools reopened and Palm Beach County schools remained open, except for West Boca High School, which is closed because of heavy flooding in the parking lot.

Still, the kitchen crew kept the operation moving.“We're still getting the job done,” Schiff said. “I have great staff over here, supporting staff with Ms. Shiel, great crew, so everything is worthwhile knowing how it's going to feed people.”The work extended beyond the turkeys.Recipes for Success graduate Ronin Nance was helping portion stuffing into 20-ounce containers, repeating the process meal after meal.“Repetition is the key to learning,” Nance said.Giving families more than a mealExtraordinary Charities board member Cassius Johnson said the families being served are neighbors dealing with the pressure of rising costs.For Johnson, putting food on the table gives families an opportunity to continue a Thanksgiving tradition centered on togetherness.“This is our opportunity to give them the food that's around that table so they can continue with an amazing tradition,” Johnson said. “One of my favorite holidays where we can just give gratitude and give thanks and spark of joy among ourselves.”And even members of the board are part of the hands-on effort. Johnson spent part of the preparation working on cranberry sauce.With all 400 meals claimed and volunteer needs filled, Extraordinary Charities says financial contributions are the remaining way for people to support this year's Turkey Takeaway. entry.title: Hobe Sound singer gets surprise duet with 'Glee' star after FAA ground stop upends his show - WFLX
entry.summary: Hobe Sound singer gets surprise duet with 'Glee' star after FAA ground stop upends his show    WFLX
entry.article_text: Last week’s FAA ground stop uprooted plans and wreaked havoc for so many people across the U.S. But for one Hobe Sound woman, it led to what could be her big break. When the FAA grounded flights across the U.S., it cast a dark cloud over the Maltz Jupiter Theatre, where Broadway and “Glee” star Matthew Morrison was scheduled to perform this weekend. Much of his ensemble couldn’t make it here. But with storms come rainbows. And one local singer can attest. Emily Rynasko, who said she watched “Glee” when she was younger, said she would have never expected a text from the actor who played William Schuester, asking her to sing a duet with him on stage. “I found out about 9:30 in the morning, and the show was at 7:30 that night,” Emily Rynasko said. It was a moment Rynasko had been working toward her whole life. “Learning sight-reading music and just using my ear. It’s being a trained musician that’s part of your job,” Rynasko said. Rynasko, who grew up in Hobe Sound, started that training as a kid at the Maltz Jupiter Theatre. The Maltz Jupiter Theater is my, my home, and that is truly my family. They have made me the woman I am,” Rynasko said. So when Rynasko stepped into the spotlight to sing Somewhere Over the Rainbow, she treated it like a professional and felt right at home next to Morrison. “I was a lot calmer than I thought I would be because I treated it like any other show that I had done,” Rynasko said. After all, there’s no place like home. “To also honor everyone that has been part of your journey, whether it’s been a teacher, your community, your friends and family,” Rynasko said. “That’s what brings me joy and carries me through.” This story was reported on-air by journalist Jamie Ostroff and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Our editorial team verifies all reporting on all platforms for fairness and accuracy.

entry.article_text: Cars were still getting through when CBS12 News reached one of the spots Port St. Lucie police had flagged for high water Thursday. Water pooled along Port St. Lucie Boulevard, and nearby driveways were dry. Earlier, water had made a lane impassable in two places on Village Parkway, and crews were pumping it off Tradition Parkway. Two weeks ago, floodwater stranded drivers across the city. Near Oak Hammock K 8, video showed a mother and daughter wading through chest-deep water. Lucie recorded 16.7 inches of rain over 60 hours during that storm. Where police reported flooding Port St. Lucie Boulevard: Crews were putting up barricades at McCorkle Avenue, at Alcantara Boulevard and along the stretch from Southwest Liberty Drive to Firestone. Northbound Village Parkway: The right lane was impassable south of the fire station and south of Discovery Way. Water was spreading into a second lane near Discovery Way. Tradition Parkway east of Hazel Drive: Crews were pumping water off the road after the outside lanes flooded in both directions. Police said more closures could be needed as rain continued. The Florida Department of Transportation also had overnight closures scheduled this week on Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Southwest Fisherman and Southwest Liberty avenues for drainage work tied to a widening project. entry.title: Port St. Lucie extends boil water notice for 21,000 customers after main break
entry.summary: About 21,000 customers in Port St. Lucie remain under a precautionary boil water notice after a contractor damaged a water main earlier this week. The city announced it is extending the notice for the Tradition and west Port St. Lucie areas following Tuesday's water main break near Glades Cut Off Road. The notice covers all of Tradition, including Western Grove, Riverland, Wilson Grove and Southern Grove, as well as areas west of Interstate 95 south to Becker Road. Communities along Glades Cut Off Road, including Copper Creek, Wylder and Verano, are also affected. City officials said the notice will remain in place until water quality testing is successfully completed and the city determines it is safe to lift. With an estimated 21,000 customers affected, officials said a significant number of water samples must be collected and tested to ensure the water is safe. The city is asking residents not to tamper with clearly marked hydrants or pipes that are flushing water, warning that interference could delay testing and extend the notice. According to officials, the break was caused by a contractor working on a construction project unrelated to the city. Crews responded and repaired the damaged 36-inch water main within hours before beginning the required flushing process. The city is investigating the incident and expects to pursue appropriate action to recover costs from those responsible. There is no estimated time for when the boil water notice will be lifted. Residents can find updates at CityofPSL.com .

entry.title: Man found guilty of murder in 2023 Riviera Beach shooting of woman
entry.summary: A jury has found a man guilty of first-degree murder in connection with the 2023 shooting of a Riviera Beach woman who remained on life support for months before dying from her injuries. Christopher Lane Jr. was convicted of first-degree murder with a firearm and shooting into an occupied vehicle in the death of Lauren St. Fort, according to the Riviera Beach Police Department. The shooting happened March 11, 2023, in the 1400 block of West 36th Street. When officers arrived, they found 27-year-old St. Fort inside her car with two gunshot wounds, one near the base of her neck and another in her thigh. Investigators said the shooting was connected to a drug deal. Witnesses told police they saw a man flag down St. Fort's car before forcing his way into the driver's side. They heard him demand, 'give me that,' followed by several gunshots. The man then ran away, witnesses told investigators. St. Fort was rushed to St. Mary's Medical Center, where she remained on a ventilator after being paralyzed from the neck down. In April 2023, family members and community supporters organized a fundraiser to help pay for her mounting medical expenses and long-term care. Her sisters said at the time that as long as she kept fighting for her life, they would keep fighting for her. Lane was arrested in May 2023, about two months after the shooting. Investigators said fingerprints recovered from St. Fort's car matched his. St. Fort remained on life support for months before dying from her injuries on Jan. 9, 2024. Following her death, the case was referred to the State Attorney's Office Homicide Unit for prosecution. 'We thank everyone who helped bring justice to Lauren St. Fort and her family,' Riviera Beach Police Chief Michael Coleman said in a statement. Lane remains in custody and is scheduled to be sentenced Jan. 5, 2027.

entry.title: Drivers caught in recent floodwaters are dealt another blow from costly mistake
entry.summary: Even though the latest round of flooding is tapering off, the problems are only beginning for drivers whose cars were flooded. Rosalie Barrios is learning a costly lesson, the hard way. Barrios says she had no idea her car was about to be overtaken by water when she was driving home from her nursing job earlier this month. When she turned into her neighborhood, the water seemed manageable, until it wasn't. 'All of a sudden the car just sank, the water came in, and I was panicking,' said Barrios. Within hours, her car conked out. The engine was waterlogged and ruined. Ron Katz, owner and mechanic of a MIDAS location in West Palm Beach, said nearly 10 gallons of water seeped into Barrios' engine. He flushed it out, but says the car was too far gone. Since the beginning of the month, Katz has serviced a handful of flooded cars. He's only been able to save one. He said the biggest mistake drivers make when they get caught in floodwaters is not letting it be and calling a tow truck. 'Human nature is, you're going to try and start your car, but the engine will hydrolock from the water being in the engine, and it'll just blow a hole through the engine,' says Katz. Katz has taken to social media this month to warn readers not to try and start their vehicles if they find themselves trapped in high water. It's something Barrios wishes she'd known. She says her insurance company declared her car a total loss. Because she still owes on it, she's now underwater again. 'I invested a lot of money, and the car was running fine. Now I'm lost. I have nothing again,' says Barrios.

entry.title: Martin County School Board rescinds termination of teacher Matthew Theobald for his comments on Charlie Kirk - WPBF
entry.summary: Martin County School Board rescinds termination of teacher Matthew Theobald for his comments on Charlie Kirk    WPBF
entry.article_text: The Martin County School Board voted this week to reinstate Matthew Theobald, a teacher at Spectrum Academy, after a judge ruled his social media posts about conservative activist Charlie Kirk’s death did not justify suspension or termination. Theobald was initially targeted by the Martin County School District for several online comments following Kirk’s murder in Utah in September 2025. The school board voted to suspend Theobald without pay and recommended his termination. Both parties agreed to an administrative hearing to address the matter. In June, the judge ruled that the school board failed to prove Theobald engaged in immorality or willful neglect of duty, which would have been grounds for dismissal. The judge also stated that Theobald’s Facebook comments did not disrupt his students, the learning environment, or reduce any teacher’s ability to teach. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Martin County School District leadership responded to the ruling by saying it would review the judge’s recommendation. This week, the school board officially voted to adopt the judge’s recommendation, rescinding Theobald’s suspension and termination. He will also be awarded back pay and benefits through June 30. School board member Marsha Powers said she voted in favor of the decision but explained her reasoning. “I have serious concerns about the process that brought this matter before a judge who does not live or work in the community,” Powers said. Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app. Board member Tony Anderson responded to Powers’ comments, saying he understood her concerns but noted the board had already placed the issue in the judge’s hands. “It’s a decision we have to live with,” Anderson said. WPBF 25 reached out to Matthew Theobald for comment but has not yet received a response.

entry.title: Vero Beach residents face another round of rising water - WFLX
entry.summary: Vero Beach residents face another round of rising water    WFLX
entry.article_text: Residents in Indian River County are dealing with another round of flooding, with approximately 12 roads closed Thursday evening and the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office urging drivers to stay off the roads as water continues to impact neighborhoods. The latest flooding comes just weeks after another round of high water left parts of the Treasure Coast struggling with similar conditions. Residents say this time, however, some neighborhoods appear to have fared better. For Terry Holly, who moved to the area from Pennsylvania with his wife 23 years ago, the flooding is an unwelcome reminder of what comes with living in Florida. “I escaped the snow to this,” Holly said. Water has surrounded parts of his neighborhood, Vero Lake Estates, leaving some residents with limited ways to get around. “We’re stuck another week. Luckily, we’ve got plenty of groceries and water, so we’re all set,” Holly said. Holly said he and other residents previously dropped their flood insurance policies. But after experiencing repeated flooding, he is reconsidering that decision. And we haven’t had it since, but now I’m going to rethink it again,” he said. County officials report multiple road closures along Vero Lake Estates. The Sheriff’s Office is urging drivers to avoid unnecessary travel and stay off flooded roads. Holly said he has not seen vehicles become stranded during this latest round of flooding, unlike the previous event. However, he warned that smaller vehicles may struggle to get through standing water. “The trucks and the high vehicles can get through. The small cars, forget it,” he said. Marjorie Hale said she believes this round of flooding has been handled better than the previous one, with more precautions being taken. But she is concerned about drivers who continue traveling too quickly through flooded neighborhoods. “You’ve got a lot of people who just don’t know how to drive in floodwaters,” Hale said. She also worries about the impact waves from passing vehicles can have on nearby homes, particularly older properties. Hale’s neighborhood experienced flooding during the previous round, too. A comparison of conditions outside her home then and now shows how the water has changed. She said drivers should slow down and consider the people living along those flooded streets. Indian River County Public Schools will be closed Friday as flooding continues to affect the area. For some families, the closure means an early start to Thanksgiving break. Hale said her daughter is old enough to stay home while she goes to work. She is also trying to find some humor in the situation. “We get our own private island. That’s what happens when it floods 6 inches of rainfall,” Hale said. Even her dog knows to be cautious around the water. He doesn’t wander off because he’s not willing to get in the floodwaters. While some residents are finding ways to make the best of the situation, Hale recognizes that other families across the Treasure Coast are dealing with more serious flooding and damage to their homes. Her message to the community is simple: look out for one another. “Invite your neighbors to Thanksgiving,” Hale said. She hopes the latest flooding will bring people together, especially those who may need a helping hand. “So let’s join together as a community,” she said. entry.article_text: The Indian River County Sheriff’s Office is reporting more flooded roads in the Vero Lake Estates area as heavy rain moves through the county Thursday. The sheriff’s office urged drivers to stay off flooded roads, warning that water can be deeper than it appears and can stall vehicles. High-water vehicles are in the area, and anyone who becomes stranded should call 911. Ryan Lloyd, Indian River County’s emergency management chief, told CBS12 News the county has received about 5 to 7 inches of rain so far. He said the north end of the county, including Sebastian, Fellsmere and Vero Lake Estates, has gotten more than the rest. Another 3 to 5 inches is expected by midnight Friday, Lloyd said, and the area is still at risk for pockets of 10 to 12 inches or more falling in a short time. Lloyd said the county’s water management systems are full and the ground is essentially saturated, so new rain is running off onto roads. The county’s emergency operations center is at a Level 2 partial activation, and National Guard members are there with high-water vehicles. Lloyd said there had been no requests for high-water rescues as of Thursday afternoon. He urged residents to avoid nonessential travel, turn around at flooded roads and never drive around barricades. Please do not drive to neighborhoods that are flooded because that can actually push floodwaters into homes and create a bigger problem than what some of those residents may already be facing, Lloyd said. The weather prompted the School District of Indian River County to close all public schools and district offices Thursday. The district said saturated ground and expected rain could make travel unsafe for students and staff. Lloyd said schools will also be closed Friday. A Vero Beach football game scheduled for Friday night has been moved to Saturday at 7 p.m., he said. CHIME IN: Send in your weather photos and videos The National Weather Service issued a flood advisory Thursday morning for eastern Indian River and northeastern St. Lucie counties, reporting that 2 to 4 inches of rain had fallen in parts of the area. The advisory warned of minor flooding in low-lying and poorly drained areas. A flood watch remains in effect for Indian River County through Friday evening, with more showers and thunderstorms possible. See also: Flood risk lingers across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beaches before a drier weekend The county’s road closure map , viewed at 2:47 p.m. Thursday, listed 13 road closures and six lane closures. Among the roads marked closed were 100th Court, 103rd Avenue, 104th Avenue, 83rd Street and 87th Street. The map also showed a long-term closure on 13th Street Southwest, scheduled to remain in place until Jan. Lane-closure listings included 101st Avenue, West 98th Avenue and two locations near Barber Street and U.S. The county also warned that heavy rain and gusty winds could disrupt trash collection. Residents whose streets are flooded were asked not to put carts in the water; the landfill and customer convenience centers could close early if conditions become unsafe. The City of Fellsmere also urged drivers to use extreme caution, identifying two potential trouble spots: New York Avenue near Hickory Street and North Broadway. The city said those roads could close if rain continues. City Hall remains open and operating normally. Lloyd said there are no known water main breaks or significant power outages in the county. The county’s Emergency Information Center, at 772-226-4000, will be open overnight Thursday for questions and flooding reports, and the county will decide Friday whether to keep it running. Residents can report flood damage to homes and businesses through the county’s emergency management website .
